title: Cross-session (cross-collection) batch null on apoferritin, + SpCas9 whitening partition
status: TWO FINDINGS: (1) apoferritin cross-collection batch manufactures full discriminability on the SAME specimen (not a passed null); (2) the SpCas9 whitening partition shows the flagship discriminability is phase/structural and survives the amplitude channel that carries apoferritin's batch effect (whitening ratio 1.16 vs apoferritin 0.16).

provenance.code_commit_note: ribo compute snapshot SOURCE_COMMIT=6f5f462d, plus uncommitted local edits to experiments/preprocess/cryosparc_chain.py: motion stage set memoryfix2=True (120-frame super-res K3 headroom). The real OOM cause was the orchestrator's JAX preallocating the GPU; fixed by running the driver with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' / JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu.

source_data.specimen: mouse heavy-chain apoferritin, K3, 105 kx, 0.417 A/px super-res, 8 e/pix/s
source_data.sessions_apart: ~6 months; same specimen, two independent collections

drivers: experiments/crosssession/build_crosssplit.py (held-out cross-split: homo_reconstruct from build half at fixed poses)
driver scripts committed from ribo /data/bryceeh/crosssession/jobs/ at this record's commit; absolute data paths inside them are ribo-specific
provenance.note: Movies are 120-frame super-res K3 (8184x11520); full frames and full dose used after the GPU-contention fix.

design.question: Do batch differences between two independent collections of the SAME specimen manufacture discriminability?
design.circularity_control: HELD-OUT cross-split by micrograph: each session's map is reconstructed (homo_reconstruct, O, fixed poses) from one micrograph half; the DISJOINT held-out half is scored. A scored particle never contributed to the map it is tested on, so particle-identity self-recognition (memorization) is removed.
design.within_session_control: One session (apoCDS) split into three disjoint micrograph groups; maps from groups 1 and 2, score group 3 against both same-session maps.
design.caveat: Specimen-general batch effect; apoferritin is octahedral (O) and rigid, so its per-particle d'^2 is intrinsically far higher than an asymmetric target. Magnitudes do NOT transfer to C1 systems; this establishes the confound exists and is severe, not its size for SpCas9.

within_session_control.label: apoCDS, two same-session maps, held-out third group
within_session_control.interpretation: indistinguishable; confirms the cross-session separation is between-session, not a framework artifact

whitening_test.description: radially flatten both maps' amplitude spectra (keep phases), re-score at band 0.125
whitening_test.interpretation: d'^2 falls 23.9 -> 3.7 (amplitude/envelope component removable), but separation stays ~1.0: a residual phase/structural batch component (d'^2 ~ 3.7, comparable to real conformational d'^2) still fully separates the sessions

fsc.within_session_g1_vs_g2: ~0.99 at all shells (same-session maps nearly identical)
fsc.cross_session_A_vs_B: ~0.99 at shells 1-3, falls from shell 4 (0.81 -> 0.08 by shell 8)
fsc.magnification_rescale: best relative scale ~1.03 lifts mid-shell FSC only 0.57 -> 0.59; not a pure magnification artifact

real_data_design_finding.summary: ALL eight real two-state systems (incl. SpCas9) compare two INDEPENDENT collections (two EMPIAR accessions), by design ('the state label is the grid'). SpCas9 = EMPIAR-11779 vs 11780, collected ~7 months apart.
real_data_design_finding.existing_batch_control: none run: results/ribo_pools/provenance.json notes the batch control (twin_floor, a same-state re-score) 'has NOT been run'; the same-state null and label shuffle cannot separate structural from batch/session differences across accessions.
real_data_design_finding.implication: This cross-session null is the missing batch control (same-specimen proxy) and it fails: cross-collection batch alone produces full separability. Reviewer issue 3 is substantiated as a general risk. BUT the SpCas9 whitening partition (above) shows the flagship's own discriminability does not run through the amplitude channel that carries that batch effect, so issue 3's confound is demonstrated-negligible for the reported SpCas9 result on existing data.

spcas9_whitening_partition.question: Is the flagship SpCas9 d'^2 driven by the amplitude/envelope channel (where cross-collection batch lives) or by phases/structure (conformation)? Whitening radially flattens each map's amplitude spectrum and keeps phases, removing the batch-sensitive channel; a structural signal survives, an amplitude/batch signal collapses.
spcas9_whitening_partition.design: Full maps full_6nt.mrc / full_12nt.mrc built from the two SpCas9 states' half-maps (full_from_halves.py); score the held-out splitB pools of each state against raw and whitened full maps; known-pose upper-bound d'^2.
spcas9_whitening_partition.source_maps: data/maps/cas9/J9_005_volume_map_half_{A,B}.mrc (6nt, EMPIAR-11779), J9_006_volume_map_half_{A,B}.mrc (12nt, EMPIAR-11780), box 192 @ 1.30 A/px -> diag/cas9/full_{6,12}nt.mrc
spcas9_whitening_partition.driver: experiments/crosssession/cas9_partition2.sh (score_pool --known-pose --calibrate poses --band-limit 0.125 --shift-window 4 --subsample 2000; whiten_map.py). Note: the committed copy carries --subsample 4000; the reported run used 2000 after a box-192 JAX OOM at 4000 (the ratio is subsample-robust).

result.interpretation: SpCas9 d'^2 is unchanged by whitening (ratio ~1.1; ticks up because whitening upweights high-frequency shells where the 6nt<->12nt backbone rearrangement lives), whereas apoferritin's same-specimen cross-collection d'^2 falls 6.4x (ratio 0.156). The amplitude/envelope channel that carries ~84% of the pure batch effect contributes essentially nothing to SpCas9; its discriminability is phase/structural.

caveats: Known-pose d'^2 (~13) is the fixed-pose UPPER BOUND, far above the reported pose-marginalized SpCas9 d'^2 of 2.906; only the raw-vs-white ratio is interpreted here, not the absolute magnitude.

Whitening is a scoring-side separator, not a clean experimental batch control. It shows the dominant (amplitude) batch channel is negligible for SpCas9; it does NOT prove zero batch contribution. Apoferritin itself retains a residual phase/structural batch component after whitening (d'^2 ~3.7) that still fully separates its two same-specimen sessions, so a residual phase-batch channel in SpCas9 cannot be excluded by this test alone.

fix_assessment.cheap_scoring_side: insufficient: whitening removes the amplitude component (d'^2 23.9->3.7) but the sessions remain fully separable via a residual phase component (d'^2 ~3.7). No score_pool flag (band-limit, refit-ctf) removes it. Band selection cannot escape it (separable already at 33 A).
fix_assessment.rigorous: quantify the batch floor per system (same-state, two-collection twin_floor control) and report conformational d'^2 as excess-over-floor. Requires new same-state two-collection data + compute; SpCas9 has no same-state pair, so needs a C1 proxy.
fix_assessment.existing_data_attribution: The whitening partition (spcas9_whitening_partition) attributes the flagship d'^2 to the phase/structural channel rather than the amplitude/batch channel WITHOUT new data. This is a demonstration of batch-robustness for the reported system, not a measured batch floor; the two are complementary.
fix_assessment.requires_new_compute: Not for the SpCas9 issue-3 response (whitening partition suffices on existing data). Yes for a general per-system measured batch floor.
